articles.fullText:
Spanish forces escort migrants to the Ceuta-Morocco border gate in the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta, August 1, 2026. 
A recent surge of undocumented migrants crossing from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta has triggered one of the most serious border crises Spain has faced in recent years, placing renewed pressure on migration management and exposing divisions within the European Union (EU).
The influx prompted Madrid to deploy military support, tighten border controls and enhance coordination with Rabat, while reigniting debate within the EU over how to manage migration at its external borders.
What's special with Ceuta?
Ceuta is one of Spain's two exclaves on the North African coast, alongside Melilla. Although geographically located in Africa, it forms part of the EU's external border.
Its location has long made it one of Europe's most sensitive migration gateways. For years, undocumented migrants have attempted to reach the enclave by climbing border fences or swimming around coastal barriers before trying to continue to mainland Spain and other parts of Europe.
Spain and Morocco have expanded cooperation in recent years on border control, migrant returns and efforts to combat human trafficking and smuggling networks.
What triggered surge?
In late June and early July, Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants intercepted at sea near Ceuta and Melilla could not be summarily returned under the special "pushback" regime applied at land borders. Instead, they must go through standard legal procedures that provide access to legal assistance and the opportunity to apply for international protection.
The ruling was quickly distorted online into claims that anyone who reached Ceuta by sea would automatically be allowed to stay in Spain and eventually obtain legal residency. The narrative spread rapidly across various social media platforms, leading many to believe the route was effectively open.
Abdellah, a Moroccan who attempted to reach Ceuta but was later turned back by police, said videos circulating online had convinced him to make the journey.
Mohammed Zakaria Aboudahab, a professor of public law and political science at Mohammed V University in Morocco, said migrant-smuggling networks had deliberately amplified false information on social media, creating the impression that reaching Ceuta guaranteed legal status.
Migrants sit outside a short-stay migrant center in the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta, August 1, 2026. 
The latest influx saw more than 50,000 undocumented migrants enter Ceuta, many by swimming around the Tarajal border crossing or using makeshift flotation devices. At least 67 people died during the crossings, with the death toll expected to rise as search and recovery operations continue.
By August 1, more than 48,000 migrants had returned to Morocco. None were allowed to travel onward to mainland Spain under Ceuta's special Schengen arrangements, and authorities said the immediate pressure at the border had largely eased.
Spain has since reinforced security by installing a new floating maritime barrier along Ceuta's breakwater. The 500-meter inflatable barrier is designed to prevent migrants from bypassing land border controls by sea.
At the same time, Madrid and Rabat have intensified cooperation on returns and law enforcement while stepping up efforts against migrant-smuggling networks.
Moroccan authorities said they had arrested 70 people suspected of organizing or participating in violence linked to the mass crossing. Xinhua reporters in Rabat and Casablanca also observed tighter security at railway stations and bus terminals, where police were screening and, when necessary, turning back groups of young people heading toward northern Morocco.
EU and regional reactions
The crisis has once again exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy.
The European Commission reaffirmed that Ceuta forms part of the EU's external border and said the bloc stands ready to support Spain through Frontex and other mechanisms while strengthening cooperation with Morocco.
Italy was among the first countries to criticize Spain's migration policy. It later joined Denmark in leading a letter signed by 22 EU member states calling for an emergency ministerial meeting to discuss the crisis and the bloc's external border management.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez responded by writing to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, expressing "serious concern" over what he described as "selfish," politically motivated reactions from some governments that he said violated EU law, including proposals to suspend Schengen cooperation with Spain. He also called for an EU-wide ministerial meeting.
Ireland, which currently holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU, subsequently announced that EU interior ministers would hold a videoconference on Tuesday to discuss the Ceuta crisis.

articles.title: Scientists reveal how aging weakens the brain's protective barrier
articles.titleCn: 科学家揭示衰老如何削弱大脑的保护屏障
articles.summary: Scientists reveal how aging weakens the brain's protective barrier
articles.summaryCn: 研究发现衰老通过TGF-β1信号增加脑内皮细胞转运，导致血脑屏障渗漏，为认知衰退提供新机制。

paragraphs.en:
As people age, many experience memory {{0}} and slower {{1}} processing, along with a higher risk of {{2}} disease and cognitive {{3}}. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline. Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a {{4}} by which aging {{5}} the blood-brain barrier, the brain's {{6}} {{7}} with the bloodstream. The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier {{9}} during aging."
The study shows how aging {{8}} transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a {{10}} security system.
paragraphs.cn: 随着人们年龄增长，许多人会经历记忆力下降和认知处理速度变慢，同时患脑血管疾病和认知障碍的风险也会增加。衰老研究中的一个重要问题是大脑血管的变化如何导致认知衰退。中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院（SIAT）的科学家们识别出衰老削弱血脑屏障（大脑与血液之间的保护性界面）的一种机制。该研究发表在《神经元》杂志上，标题为“TGF-β1诱导的内皮转胞吞作用驱动衰老过程中的血脑屏障渗漏”。该研究展示了衰老如何扰乱脑血管细胞中的运输，导致血脑屏障渗漏。/SIAT 血脑屏障（BBB）像一个选择性安全系统。

paragraphs.en: It allows {{11}} nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially {{12}} substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several {{13}} disorders. Scientists have traditionally {{14}} BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging. By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already {{15}} in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals.
paragraphs.cn: 它允许必需营养物质到达大脑，同时防止血液中潜在有害物质进入脑组织。这种屏障的损伤与认知衰老、脑小血管疾病和多种神经退行性疾病有关。科学家传统上将BBB渗漏主要归因于脑内血管内皮细胞之间紧密连接的损伤。然而，新研究发现另一个过程在衰老过程中更早发生。通过检查不同年龄的小鼠，研究人员发现BBB渗漏在中年小鼠中已可检测到，并在老年动物中恶化。

paragraphs.en: The change appeared early in the {{16}}, a brain region important for learning and memory. At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely {{17}}. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became {{18}} active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue. "Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said. The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system.
paragraphs.cn: 这种变化早期出现在海马体，这是一个对学习和记忆重要的大脑区域。在这个阶段，血管细胞之间的连接基本保持完整。相反，细胞内部的运输系统变得异常活跃，允许血液中的物质穿过细胞进入脑组织。“衰老的血脑屏障似乎不是首先通过细胞间隙渗漏，而是失去了对细胞内运输途径的控制，”研究人员说。团队识别出一种名为Mfsd2a的蛋白质，它是这个保护系统的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased. When the researchers {{19}} endothelial Mfsd2a expression or knocked down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced. articles.fullText:
As people age, many experience memory decline and slower cognitive processing, along with a higher risk of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive impairment. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline.
Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a mechanism by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective interface with the bloodstream.
The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier leakage during aging."
The study shows how aging disrupts transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a selective security system. It allows essential nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially harmful substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several neurodegenerative disorders.
Scientists have traditionally attributed BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging.
By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already detectable in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals. The change appeared early in the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory.
At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely intact. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became abnormally active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue.
"Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said.
The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system. Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased.
When the researchers restored endothelial Mfsd2a expression or knocked down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced.
The researchers then investigated why Mfsd2a declines during aging. They found that levels of TGF-β1, a signaling molecule involved in inflammation, tissue repair and aging, increased in both the brain and the bloodstream as mice aged.
Excessive TGF-β1 reduced Mfsd2a expression in the cells lining brain blood vessels, causing their transport activity to increase. Raising TGF-β1 levels in young mice caused them to develop several features normally seen in the aged BBB, including increased leakage.
By contrast, blocking TGF-β signaling in aged mice reduced BBB leakage and improved their performance in memory-related behavioral tests.
The findings suggest that age-related BBB damage is not simply the result of passive wear and tear. Instead, it involves biological signals that alter how brain blood vessel cells transport substances.
The study may help explain how vascular changes contribute to cognitive aging. It also points to potential approaches for protecting the aging brain, including maintaining Mfsd2a function or preventing excessive activation of TGF-β signaling. Further research will be needed to determine whether these strategies can be safely translated into treatments for humans.

随着人们年龄增长，许多人会经历记忆力下降和认知处理速度变慢，同时患脑血管疾病和认知障碍的风险也会增加。衰老研究中的一个重要问题是大脑血管的变化如何导致认知衰退。中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院（SIAT）的科学家们识别出衰老削弱血脑屏障（大脑与血液之间的保护性界面）的一种机制。该研究发表在《神经元》杂志上，标题为“TGF-β1诱导的内皮转胞吞作用驱动衰老过程中的血脑屏障渗漏”。该研究展示了衰老如何扰乱脑血管细胞中的运输，导致血脑屏障渗漏。/SIAT 血脑屏障（BBB）像一个选择性安全系统。

它允许必需营养物质到达大脑，同时防止血液中潜在有害物质进入脑组织。这种屏障的损伤与认知衰老、脑小血管疾病和多种神经退行性疾病有关。科学家传统上将BBB渗漏主要归因于脑内血管内皮细胞之间紧密连接的损伤。然而，新研究发现另一个过程在衰老过程中更早发生。通过检查不同年龄的小鼠，研究人员发现BBB渗漏在中年小鼠中已可检测到，并在老年动物中恶化。

这种变化早期出现在海马体，这是一个对学习和记忆重要的大脑区域。在这个阶段，血管细胞之间的连接基本保持完整。相反，细胞内部的运输系统变得异常活跃，允许血液中的物质穿过细胞进入脑组织。“衰老的血脑屏障似乎不是首先通过细胞间隙渗漏，而是失去了对细胞内运输途径的控制，”研究人员说。团队识别出一种名为Mfsd2a的蛋白质，它是这个保护系统的重要组成部分。

Mfsd2a通常限制大脑血管上的不必要运输。其水平随年龄增长而下降，而参与运输囊泡形成的Caveolin-1蛋白则增加。当研究人员在老年小鼠中恢复内皮Mfsd2a表达或敲低Caveolin-1时，异常囊泡运输和BBB渗漏显著减少。研究人员随后调查了为什么Mfsd2a在衰老过程中下降。他们发现，随着年龄增长，小鼠大脑和血液中TGF-β1（一种参与炎症、组织修复和衰老的信号分子）的水平增加。

过量的TGF-β1降低了脑内血管内皮细胞中Mfsd2a的表达，导致其运输活性增加。在年轻小鼠中提高TGF-β1水平，使它们出现通常见于老年BBB的多种特征，包括渗漏增加。相反，在老年小鼠中阻断TGF-β信号减少了BBB渗漏，并改善了它们在记忆相关行为测试中的表现。这些发现表明，与年龄相关的BBB损伤不仅仅是被动磨损的结果。相反，它涉及改变脑血管细胞运输物质的生物信号。

这项研究可能有助于解释血管变化如何导致认知衰老。它还指出了保护衰老大脑的潜在方法，包括维持Mfsd2a功能或防止TGF-β信号的过度激活。需要进一步研究来确定这些策略是否能安全地转化为人类治疗方法。

The fires that have ravaged France are "today under control," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Saturday, more than a week after the country's largest wildfire since 1949 flared up.
"Overall, the fires are now under control in our country," he said in an interview with the La Tribune Dimanche weekly.
The largest wildfire erupted more than a week ago in a pine forest near the southwestern city of Bordeaux.
"We have returned to a more stable situation," Lecornu said, confirming earlier comments by Interior Minister Laurent Nunez.
France has for weeks been battling wildfires after a series of deadly heatwaves that have dried up riverbeds and vegetation, extreme weather events scientists have linked to human-made climate change.
In the Gironde region near the winemaking capital of Bordeaux, an inferno ripped through 42,000 hectares of pine forest along the Atlantic coastline – an area larger than the US city of Detroit. It also destroyed around 240 homes.
Some local people think a brushwood-clearing machine accidentally started the blaze with a spark on July 29.
Sophie Brocas, the prefect of the southwestern Gironde region, remained cautious on Saturday.
"Fire fixed doesn't mean fire out," she warned, mentioning two "hot points" still giving cause for concern.
But most of the 224,000 people evacuated from the flames have been allowed to return to their homes, she said.
She said the others would have to wait for the fire to be put out in the areas where it was still active.
Most land burnt in years
An aircraft flies over a wildfire near Lanton, east of the Arcachon Bay, west of Bordeaux, during wildfires in the Gironde region, southwestern France, July 29, 2026. 
Lecornu, in his interview, made it clear that if the situation changed, the authorities would take the appropriate action.
The fire in the southeastern Var region was still under close surveillance, he added.
Firefighters there have managed to stem the advance of a fast-moving blaze that sprang up Friday, said regional prefect Simon Babre.
Strong winds fanning the flames had caused them to spread "faster than a galloping horse," he said, warning that the situation was still "extremely precarious."
"We're staying cautious because the fight goes on," he added.
The fire was just the latest of several that have consumed 5,600 hectares of land in total in the region in July. Hollywood star George Clooney, his wife Amal and children were among those forced to flee their home earlier this week.
Rail traffic, interrupted since last weekend south of Bordeaux, finally resumed on Saturday as another wave of holidaymakers started or finished their summer breaks.
The wildfire near Bordeaux is the largest nationwide since a deadly forest fire in the same region in 1949, which scorched around 50,000 hectares.
Lecornu, in his interview, encouraged people to go on holiday in the region as "a gesture of solidarity."
The total area of land burnt so far this year in France – 92,000 hectares – is the largest on record for any year over the past 20 years, according to satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System.
Elsewhere in France, a fire in the Fontainebleau forest near Paris incinerated a tenth of the UNESCO-listed site in mid-July, after several other wildfires in the country.
